dialog.body: Recreation Department, this is Beth, happy holidays. How can I help you?
Hey Beth, happy holidays to you too. David here. Um, can you hear me okay? I'm on speakerphone, I've got both hands full of a sandwich situation.
I can hear you fine. Go right ahead, enjoy your sandwich.

Ha, thanks. So, I'm calling about the beach parks. Like the ones along the water, Easton's, or any of the little ones. My sister is coming in from out of state for the holiday and she wants to take a walk down by the water, and I said, sure, sure, but I don't actually know when they close this time of year.

Good question. So in the winter, the beach areas are generally open during daylight hours, dawn to dusk, more or less. This time of year the sun goes down pretty early, so you'd want to plan on being done by around four-thirty or so.

Four-thirty. Wow, okay. Yeah, that's early. See, that's what I was worried about, because she doesn't land until, hang on, what's it, she lands at like two-something, and then it's the whole thing with the rental car, and last year the rental car place had a line out the door, and I'm not kidding, a guy in front of her was trying to return a car that had a dog in it. Not a dog, I mean, a dog's, a dog hair situation. Anyway.
[pause] Ha, okay. So she might be cutting it close.

Right, right, exactly. And honestly I'm not going to be much of a tour guide today either. I work seasonal retail, so it's the crazy season, and I've been on my feet since six this morning. I'm going to be dead by three, I swear. My feet are, like, they're their own separate people at this point.
Oh, I bet. December in retail, that's a marathon. Hang in there, you're almost through it.
Two more days, then I get a breather. Anyway, so, dusk. Is that a hard closing, like a gate, or is it more of a, you know, walk at your own risk thing?
It depends on the spot. Some have gates or posted hours, and a lot of the shoreline spots are just posted for dawn to dusk. So I'd look for a sign when you get there. If it's posted, go by that.

Okay, that makes sense. Because the one time I went to Easton's in the evening there was a sign and I totally ignored it and nobody said anything, but I don't want to be that guy in front of my sister. She's the rule follower. She's the one who alphabetized our spices when she visited once.
[pause] Ha, good to have one in every family. Well, if you get there before dusk you'll be golden.

Yeah. Okay. So, um, what if that doesn't work out? Like, say she's late, or the one we pick is closed or blocked off or whatever. Is there a plan B? Somewhere else that stays open later, or somebody I can call?

Sure. If the beach you pick is closed, the other waterfront spots and the walking paths are mostly the same daylight hours, so I'd head to another one nearby rather than count on one staying open. And if you want to double-check a particular spot, you can call us back here and we'll tell you what we know. We're here until the end of the day today.
Okay, good. And tomorrow? Christmas Eve, are you guys open?
I'd call ahead for that one, since the holiday schedule shifts. If you get the main line and nobody picks up, leave a message and someone will get back to you.

Perfect. That's really all I needed. I had this whole thing, I was going to circle back to the, hang on, yeah, the sunset thing. Right. If she wants to catch the sunset, that's a good time, right? Like four-ish?
Right around then, yes. It's a pretty time of day out there, even when it's cold. Tell her to bundle up, the wind off the water this week is no joke.
Oh, I will. She never brings a real coat. Okay, Beth, thank you so much. This was super helpful, and sorry about the sandwich noises.
No apology needed. Have a great Christmas, David, and enjoy the visit with your sister.
You too, Beth. Take care, happy holidays.
